answer.evidence: The board is rows 1-16 and 16 px wide. Row 1 is a dark outline 14 px wide. Rows 2-5 at the top are only a grey-blue frame highlight, and the frame continues down the right edge (x=11, rows 2-12), so it is a frame and not a horizontal band. The rusty face runs from the top down to row 15 with no front-edge line and no eave shadow, so the board is a vertical face with at most a 1-row rim on top. The post (rows 17-26, 5 px wide) is a vertical shaft. The small 7-9-7 px foot at rows 27-29 is a minor ellipse and is not the main body. The reference guide's 'front elevation' and 'rim only' examples match this drawing.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate shows 12 visible tones per 16x16 tile. That is above the hedge reference (9) and below the cheese stall (17) and the roofed well (20), which are larger, busier props. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans brown or rust and reads as a dark version of the adjacent material, not a black sticker line. The board face has mottled rust speckle with a lighter top edge, and the post has its own darker value. That gives roughly 5 steps on the rust and wood ramps against about 6 on the references. It is small and simple, but a careful artist would accept it beside the hedge and the stall without it looking flatter. It is slightly less rich than the best references, but not enough to fail.
